items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: that was a man named Eppie Jackson who I still say was the greatest sousaphone player in the world... But he was with one of those bands in Kansas City.

ctx.x: You know, they still had that big, heavy foot, though, which made the rhythm section--
Now where does -- what I'm trying to get at here is, when you're a tuba or a sousaphone, and the drummer was still the head man, what was really the role of the sousaphone or the tuba?
The sousaphone--first of all, he could only--he couldn't play those fast tempos. He could play as loud as that drummer. But he couldn't play full. You know, he couldn't play the--
